newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-WOODS TAKES LEAD IN TEXAS ENTERING FINAL ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS TAKES LEAD IN TEXAS ENTERING FINAL ROUND.

text.p: Tiger Woods was not at the top of his game, but he did enough to open a two-stroke lead after the third round at the $1.8 million Byron Nelson Classic on Saturday.
Woods, in his first event since his runaway win at last month's Masters, stayed on course for back-to-back victories with a three-under-par 67 on the Las Colinas TPC course.
He birdied the final hole to post a 15-under 195 total with one round to play, equalling the tournament record low 54-hole score.
Fellow-Americans David Berganio (66), Dan Forsman (66), Jim Furyk (67), Lee Rinker (69) and Mike Standly (68) were tied for second at 13-under 197, while seven others were three strokes behind.
Rinker, who shared the halfway lead with Woods, held the outright lead after 15 holes, but he was on the wrong end of a two-shot swing at the 16th.
Woods, 21, compiled six birdies and three bogeys, and he was the first to admit that he had not fired on all cylinders.
"Overall today I had good and bad. I need to work on my swing. I know what I am doing wrong," said Woods, who hit 11 greens in regulation.
"It's causing a position on my downswing which the right elbow gets stuck behind the ball. There are certain faults which will stick with you for the rest of your life.
"What's keeping me in the tournament is my short game. I'm getting up and down, often from precarious positions."
"I'm going to have to play better," Woods said. "There are so many guys who could win. All you need is someone to get a hot hand with the flat stick."
Woods birdied the fifth hole from two feet, but bogeyed the next after firing a wedge over the green.
He bounced back to birdie the next three holes from inside 10 feet, then bogeyed the 11th and 12th holes.
At the 11th he could not reach the green with his second shot after finding a fairway bunker and carelessly three-putted the 12th.
Those were his last mistakes, as he finished strongly with a birdie at the par-five 16th, where he chipped to two feet, and another birdie at the 18th, after hitting a nine-iron to five feet.
Woods improved his record to 37 under par over the past 117 holes, since slumping to four over after nine holes of the first round at the Masters.
